topic: Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz

targets.claim: The Iran conflict has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global oil and gas chokepoint, prompting warnings, market disruption, and outside efforts to keep shipping moving.
The United States said it will provide insurance guarantees and naval escorts for oil tankers and other vessels transiting the strait.
Iranian forces have issued radio warnings and reported attacks on vessels, prompting some international shipping groups to suspend sailings in the waterway.
The ongoing conflict has strained the Strait of Hormuz — the vital strategic energy and shipping chokepoint, prompting concerns, commercial pressure, and broader efforts to keep shipping moving.
The escalating conflict has constrained the Strait of Hormuz, the critical global energy and maritime chokepoint, driving concerns, shipping costs, and international measures to keep traffic moving.
Iran has called the Strait of Hormuz unsafe and warned it may strike ships attempting to cross, while U.S. Central Command maintains this route stays accessible.
The regional conflict has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz — the major strategic energy and shipping chokepoint, raising concern, oil prices, and diplomatic measures to keep shipping moving.
Iran still calls the Strait of Hormuz unsafe and warns it may target vessels trying to cross; however U.S. Central Command says the route remains open.
